label: Lipid Breakdown
summary: 27-carbon bile acid intermediates accumulate. Oral cholic acid (FDA-approved 2015) is used as add-on treatment, with caution in advanced liver disease ([Berendse 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27469511/)).
description: Peroxisomes break down fats that no other part of the cell can handle, preventing harmful build-up, and create usable molecules in the process, including bile acids (for digestion) and DHA (an omega-3 building block for the brain and retina).

parts.label: Breakdown (beta-oxidation) of Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFAs)
parts.panelTitle: Breakdown (beta-oxidation) of Very Long Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFAs)
parts.text: Peroxisomes break down VLCFAs (fatty acids 22 carbons or longer), which mitochondria cannot process, and hand the shortened products to mitochondria to finish the job.
left: **[X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** the transporter that feeds VLCFAs into the peroxisome (ABCD1) fails, so VLCFAs build up in blood and tissue and damage the adrenal glands and the brain's white matter.

**[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (PBDs)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** when peroxisomes fail to form, VLCFAs build up throughout the body. An elevated blood level of the 26-carbon fatty acid C26:0 is the standard first screening test for Zellweger spectrum disorders.

**[Single-enzyme disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** ACOX1 deficiency and D-bifunctional protein (HSD17B4) deficiency each block one step of this pathway and cause severe infantile neurological disease that closely resembles Zellweger spectrum ([Ferdinandusse 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16385454/)).
furtherReading: [Wanders 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33417207/) (pathway overview)
[Engelen 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22889154/) (X-ALD clinical overview)
[Wanders and Waterham 2006](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.biochem.74.082803.133329) (biochemistry of mammalian peroxisomes)
[Wanders 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biochi.2013.08.022) (metabolic functions of peroxisomes in health and disease)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** VLCFA oxidation fails in brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)), and VLCFAs are elevated in cortex in proportion to disease pathology ([Kou 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21594711/)).
**[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** VLCFA oxidation fails in brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).

**[Alzheimer's disease:](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease)** blocking peroxisomal beta-oxidation in rats raises VLCFAs and amyloid-beta in the brain ([Shi 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neulet.2012.08.086)).
**[Cancer:](#/diseases/cancer)** melanoma cells that survive BRAF/MEK inhibitor treatment depend on ACOX1-driven fatty acid oxidation ([Shen 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108421)).

parts.label: Breakdown (alpha-oxidation) of branched fats such as phytanic acid
parts.panelTitle: Breakdown (alpha-oxidation) of branched fats such as phytanic acid
parts.text: Phytanic acid, a branched fat from dairy, ruminant meat and some fish, carries a side branch that blocks normal fat breakdown. Peroxisomes clip off one carbon (alpha-oxidation) to make pristanic acid, which is then broken down by peroxisomal beta-oxidation.
left: **[Refsum disease](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** variants in PHYH (the alpha-oxidation enzyme) or PEX7 (the receptor that imports it) block this step. Phytanic acid builds up and causes retinitis pigmentosa (progressive vision loss), loss of smell, nerve damage and unsteady gait, typically starting in late childhood or adulthood. Restricting dietary phytanic acid is the main treatment ([Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/)).

**[AMACR deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** AMACR flips pristanic acid and bile acid intermediates into the mirror-image form that beta-oxidation enzymes can use. Its loss causes an adult-onset nerve disorder ([Ferdinandusse 2000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10655068/)).

**[PBDs and RCDP type 1](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** phytanic acid rises in both, because the alpha-oxidation enzyme depends on PEX7-mediated import. Levels also depend on diet and age, so they are less useful for diagnosis in infants.
furtherReading: [Wanders 2011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21683154/) (alpha-oxidation and disease)
right: **[Prostate cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** AMACR is elevated distinctively enough in prostate tumors to be used as a routine diagnostic marker in pathology labs ([Luo 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11956072/); [Rubin 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11926890/)), and it links this pathway to tumor growth and redox stress ([Kong 2020a](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2020.00153/full)).

**[Prostate cancer risk and diet](#/diseases/cancer):** dairy and red meat, the main dietary sources of phytanic acid, have been proposed as a link between diet and prostate cancer risk. Epidemiological evidence is limited and mixed: a small case-control study found higher serum phytanic acid in men with prostate cancer, while two larger prospective studies found no overall association ([Price 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20427733/); [Wright 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25132681/)).

parts.label: Production (beta-oxidation) of bile acids
parts.text: Peroxisomes trim the 27-carbon precursors the liver makes from cholesterol (DHCA and THCA) down to the 24-carbon bile acids (cholic and chenodeoxycholic acid) the gut uses to absorb fats and fat-soluble vitamins.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** the 27-carbon intermediates accumulate in blood and are thought to contribute to liver disease. Oral cholic acid (Cholbam) was approved by the FDA in 2015 as an add-on treatment for peroxisomal disorders including Zellweger spectrum; a clinical study found it lowered the toxic intermediates in some patients but cautioned against use in advanced liver disease ([Berendse 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27469511/)).

**[Single-enzyme disorders:](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27647924/)** AMACR, ACOX2 and D-bifunctional protein deficiencies raise the 27-carbon bile acid intermediates, and liver injury can be the presenting sign in ACOX2 deficiency (Vilarinho 2016). SCPx deficiency is different: the one reported patient had raised pristanic acid and abnormal urinary bile alcohols rather than raised 27-carbon intermediates.
furtherReading: [Ferdinandusse 2009](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17034878/) (peroxisomes in bile acid synthesis)
right: **[Liver disease](#/diseases/liver):** no common condition has yet been tied specifically to the peroxisomal steps of bile acid synthesis; these steps are linked to rare inherited disease only. Bile acid signaling is an active drug target in cholestatic and fatty liver disease, so peroxisome-specific bile acid intermediates are a candidate biomarker worth testing.

parts.label: Production (beta-oxidation) of DHA
parts.text: DHA (docosahexaenoic acid), the brain and retina's key omega-3 fat, is finished in the peroxisome: a 24-carbon precursor made in the endoplasmic reticulum is shortened by one round of peroxisomal beta-oxidation to 22-carbon DHA.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** DHA is markedly reduced in the brain and retina of patients. A randomized trial of DHA supplementation in Zellweger spectrum found no clinical benefit on vision or development ([Paker 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20805528/)).

**[D-bifunctional protein deficiency:](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11500517/)** patient cells cannot complete this final chain-shortening step, so DHA is low ([Su 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11500517/)).
furtherReading: [Ferdinandusse 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11734571/) (identifies the peroxisomal step in DHA synthesis)
[Salem 2001](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11745-001-0805-6) (how DHA acts in the nervous system)
[Belkouch 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnutbio.2016.03.002) (DHA and the hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease)
[Pan 2015](https://doi.org/10.2174/157488471003150820151532) (DHA and the blood-brain barrier in Alzheimer's disease)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** DHA-containing plasmalogens are reduced in Alzheimer's brain tissue ([Han 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11359882/)). Whether impaired peroxisomal DHA production contributes is not established.

**Retinal degeneration:** low DHA in photoreceptor membranes is linked to vision loss in genetic peroxisomal disorders. Mice lacking peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzymes develop photoreceptor and retinal pigment epithelium degeneration ([Swinkels 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37934161/)), but omega-3 supplementation did not slow progression to advanced age-related macular degeneration in the AREDS2 trial, so a contribution to common retinal disease is unproven.

label: Lipid Synthesis (Plasmalogens)
summary: plasmalogen loss tracks with cognitive decline and influences cell-death sensitivity in aging tissues ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).
description: Peroxisomes build plasmalogens, a family of membrane fats that no other part of the cell can make. An unusual chemical bond at one end (a vinyl-ether bond) lets them do two jobs at once: structural building blocks in specialized membranes, and built-in antioxidants.

parts.label: Structural role in key membranes
parts.text: Plasmalogens are unusually concentrated in the insulation around nerve fibers (myelin), heart muscle, and sperm.
left: **[Rhizomelic Chondrodysplasia Punctata (RCDP)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** caused by variants in PEX7 (type 1), GNPAT (type 2), AGPS (type 3), FAR1 (type 4) or the long isoform of PEX5 (type 5), all of which block plasmalogen synthesis. Children have shortened upper limbs, cataracts, skeletal changes and severe developmental delay present from birth ([Braverman 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22627108/)).
**[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** plasmalogens are reduced, and a low red blood cell plasmalogen level is a standard diagnostic test.
furtherReading: [Luoma 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25801291/) (plasmalogens protect nerve insulation from oxidative damage)
[Braverman 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22627108/) (functions of plasmalogens in health and disease)
[Honsho and Fujiki 2017](https://doi.org/10.1002/1873-3468.12743) (how plasmalogen synthesis is regulated)
right: **[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** plasmalogen synthesis fails in Alzheimer's brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)), alongside broader loss of nerve-insulating lipids ([Han 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11359882/)).
**[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** plasmalogen synthesis also fails in MS brain tissue ([Roczkowsky 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12426004/)).
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** plasmalogens drop in brain and blood with age, correlating with cognitive decline ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).

parts.label: Antioxidant protection
parts.text: The vinyl-ether bond in plasmalogens reacts readily with oxidants, so plasmalogens absorb oxidative damage that would otherwise strike the rest of the membrane, protecting cells from within.
left: **[RCDP and Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders)**: cells lacking plasmalogens are more vulnerable to oxidative damage. The clearest evidence comes from ether lipid-deficient cells and mouse models ([Perez 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36178986/)) rather than from patient fibroblasts.
furtherReading: [Zou 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32939090/) (peroxisome-made ether lipids and ferroptosis)
[Dean 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28523433/) (ether lipid functions)
right: **[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** the peroxisomal enzyme AGPS builds ether lipids that fuel cancer cell migration, invasion and survival signals across multiple tumor types ([Chen 2024](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51489-1)). The same ether lipids can make tumor cells more vulnerable to ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death driven by lipid oxidation (Zou 2020). This is a paradox: the property that protects healthy membranes can be a weak point in tumors.
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** falling plasmalogen levels influence cell-death sensitivity in aging tissues ([Curran 2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022227525001889)).

**[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** some enveloped viruses expand peroxisomes and take over ether lipid and plasmalogen production to build their own membranes ([Ferreira 2022](http://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0962892421001999)).

**[Parkinson's disease:](#/diseases/brain-nerve)** blood plasmalogens are lower in Parkinson's disease ([Dragonas 2009](https://doi.org/10.1515/cclm.2009.205)), and the lipid composition of frontal cortex membranes is altered ([Fabelo 2011](https://doi.org/10.2119/molmed.2011.00119)). In MPTP mice, plasmalogen augmentation and plasmalogen precursors reduce striatal dopamine loss ([Miville-Godbout 2016](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0151020); [Miville-Godbout 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.brainres.2017.08.020)).

label: Detoxification
summary: restoring the DsbA-L/catalase complex reduces kidney damage ([Liu 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213231723002562)).
description: Peroxisomes are where the cell runs its dangerous chemistry on purpose, inside a sealed container. Breaking things down generates hydrogen peroxide, which the organelle neutralizes on the spot using catalase, one of the fastest enzymes known, and it disposes of other reactive molecules the body cannot leave circulating.

parts.label: Glyoxylate disposal
parts.text: Glyoxylate is a metabolic by-product that turns into oxalate, which crystallizes into kidney stones if not cleared. The peroxisomal enzyme AGXT converts glyoxylate into the harmless amino acid glycine. Silencing glycolate oxidase, the peroxisomal enzyme that makes glyoxylate, is the basis of an approved RNA-interference drug.
left: **[Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 (PH1)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of AGXT causes oxalate to accumulate and crystallize, damaging the kidneys and, as kidney function falls, other organs.
**[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** calcium oxalate kidney stones also occur in some patients ([van Woerden 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16621644/)).
furtherReading: [Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/) (PH1 and peroxisomal enzyme targeting)
[Garrelfs 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/) (phase 3 trial of lumasiran)
right: **[Kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** most kidney stones in the general population are calcium oxalate. Lumasiran (approved by the FDA in 2020 for PH1) silences glycolate oxidase (HAO1) in the liver, making it an approved drug that works by targeting a peroxisomal enzyme ([Garrelfs 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33789010/)).

parts.label: Hydrogen peroxide neutralization
parts.text: Peroxisomal fat breakdown generates hydrogen peroxide, which catalase neutralizes in the same sealed compartment. Controlled leakage of hydrogen peroxide may also act as a signal that reports the cell's metabolic state. Peroxisomes also handle reactive nitrogen species (RNS), and the balance of these reactive molecules helps decide whether a stressed cell survives or dies.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** catalase cannot be imported and stays in the cytosol, leaving empty peroxisome membranes ('ghosts'). Catalase location in patient cells is a classic diagnostic readout.

**[Acatalasemia](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** inherited loss of catalase (CAT gene) is usually mild; some individuals develop mouth ulcers, and an increased frequency of diabetes has been reported in catalase-deficient families ([Góth 2000](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11117918/)).
furtherReading: [Lismont 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31357514/) (peroxisomal hydrogen peroxide as a signal)
[Fransen 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bbadis.2011.12.001) (peroxisomes in ROS and RNS metabolism)
[He 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcb.2021.02.005) (peroxisomes as adaptors to metabolic and environmental stress)
[Giorgio 2007](https://doi.org/10.1038/nrm2240) (hydrogen peroxide as a signal in ageing)
right: **[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** in lymphoma, peroxisomes buffer free radicals generated by cancer drugs, letting tumor cells survive otherwise lethal treatment ([Dahabieh 2017](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5635217/)).

**[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** PEX5 import defects and catalase loss compromise detoxification of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in neurodegenerative disease ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Diabetic kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** kidneys develop structurally intact but functionally 'empty' peroxisomes; loss of the DsbA-L/catalase complex disables local antioxidant defense and accelerates damage ([Liu 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213231723002562)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** in fat tissue, peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL and suppresses fat breakdown ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** declining PEX5-dependent import of catalase leaves peroxisomes as net ROS generators across multiple tissues ([Kim 2024](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/3/10/pgae429/7793200)).

parts.label: D-amino acid handling
parts.text: The peroxisomal enzyme D-amino acid oxidase (DAO) breaks down D-serine, a mirror-image amino acid that the brain uses to boost signaling through NMDA receptors, which are central to learning and memory. DAO activity helps set how much D-serine is available.
left: No human disorder caused by DAO deficiency has been described. In PBDs, DAO cannot be imported into peroxisomes; D-serine has not been measured in patients, and the consequences are hard to predict because unimported DAO can stay active in the cytosol.
furtherReading: [Terry-Lorenzo 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39756412/) (D-amino acid oxidase inhibitors in human clinical trials)
[Paul and De Belleroche 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00726-012-1385-9) (D-amino acids in ALS)
right: **Schizophrenia:** reduced NMDA receptor signaling is a leading hypothesis, and DAO inhibitors have been tested in clinical trials to raise D-serine. The DAO inhibitor luvadaxistat did not meet its primary endpoint in a phase 2 trial (Terry-Lorenzo 2024).
**ALS:** a DAO variant (R199W) was identified in a family with inherited ALS (Mitchell 2010).

label: Organelle Crosstalk
summary: weaker contacts accelerate mitochondrial breakdown and muscle aging ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).
description: Peroxisomes physically dock onto the cell's other compartments and hand material back and forth. These are not loose associations but physical tethers: specific proteins on each surface clamp the two compartments together at a defined distance.

parts.label: Mitochondria
parts.text: Peroxisomes pass partially broken-down fats to mitochondria to finish the job; mitochondria in peroxisome-deficient cells are visibly abnormal as a result.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** some of the cellular damage in peroxisomal disease is inflicted second-hand, through structurally and functionally abnormal mitochondria in peroxisome-deficient cells ([Baumgart 2001](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11583975/)).
furtherReading: [Schrader 2015a](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25687155/) (peroxisome-mitochondria interplay in disease)
[Schrader 2020](https://doi.org/10.1002/jimd.12083) (organelle interplay: peroxisome interactions in health and disease)
[Ravi 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.devcel.2021.04.019) (PI5P4Ks and peroxisome-mitochondria interplay)
[Tanaka 2019](https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.224766) (peroxisomes control mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis)
right: **[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** peroxisome positioning and contact patterns are remodeled over the course of infection, suggesting viruses may rewire peroxisome-mitochondria crosstalk to favor replication or immune evasion ([Cook 2022](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32488-6)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** aging weakens peroxisome-mitochondria contacts, disrupting lipid transfer and accelerating mitochondrial breakdown and muscle aging ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).

**[Diabetic kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** peroxisomal fat breakdown produces succinate, which disrupts mitochondrial energy production and generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) ([Wang 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8881667/)).

parts.label: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)
parts.text: Peroxisomes draw raw material from the ER, the cell's membrane-building factory. Tether proteins such as ACBD5 on the peroxisome and VAPB on the ER hold the two together so lipids can move between them.
left: **[ACBD5 deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of the peroxisome-ER tether causes retinal degeneration and white matter disease with raised VLCFAs ([Ferdinandusse 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27799409/)).

**[PBDs caused by PEX3, PEX16 or PEX19](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** these genes build the peroxisome membrane itself. Patient cells in these groups lack even the empty membrane 'ghosts' found in most other Zellweger groups ([Honsho 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9837814/)), and the presentation is usually at the severe end, though milder PEX16 cases have been reported ([Kumar 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30094183/)).
furtherReading: [Costello 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28108524/) (ACBD5-VAPB peroxisome-ER tether)
[Castro 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibs.2018.01.001) (peroxisome contact sites in disease)
right: **[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** peroxisome contacts with mitochondria and the ER help shape the lipid composition of synaptic membranes ([Carmichael 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnmol.2025.1603632/full)).
**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** aging weakens peroxisome contacts with the ER and mitochondria, disrupting lipid transfer ([Scalabrin 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64833-w)).

parts.label: Lipid droplets
parts.text: Peroxisomes tap directly into stored fat droplets for fuel. During fasting, peroxisomes move to lipid droplets and help switch on fat release.
left: No genetic peroxisomal disorder has been defined by a lipid droplet contact defect. The one disorder defined by a contact site defect, ACBD5 deficiency, involves peroxisome-ER contacts instead.
furtherReading: [Kong 2020b](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31996685/) (PEX5 brings ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contacts)
[Han 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515256420960303) (PEX5 escorts the lipase ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contacts during fasting)
[Lodhi and Semenkovich 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cmet.2014.01.002) (peroxisomes as a hub for lipid metabolism and signaling)
right: **[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** during fasting, PEX5 escorts the fat-releasing enzyme ATGL to peroxisome-lipid droplet contact sites, making these contacts important for stimulated fat breakdown ([Han 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515256420960303)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** peroxisome-derived ROS stabilize PEX2, which degrades ATGL and suppresses fat breakdown, so peroxisomes act as fatty-acid sensors that tune storage versus release ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).

label: Immune & Inflammatory Signaling
summary: in cerebral ALD, microglial damage comes before myelin loss ([Bergner 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30980503/)).
description: Peroxisomes are one of the places a cell raises the alarm when a virus gets in, and they shape how immune cells behave once inflammation starts. Several viruses have evolved to destroy or shrink peroxisomes specifically to shut this down, a sign that this defense matters.

parts.label: Immune cell behavior and inflammation
parts.text: Immune cells depend heavily on lipid handling to decide what to do, and the brain's resident immune cells (microglia) are particularly sensitive to peroxisomal failure.
left: **[Cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy (childhood cerebral ALD)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** microglial damage appears before major loss of nerve insulation, not after it, meaning inflammation is part of the disease mechanism rather than a downstream reaction ([Bergner 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30980503/)). This is why the disease is treated by replacing the patient's blood-forming stem cells, through transplant or the approved gene therapy elivaldogene autotemcel.
furtherReading: [Ferreira 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31382586/) (review of peroxisomes in innate immunity)
[Di Cara 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28723556/) (peroxisomes required for macrophage immune function)
[Di Cara 2019](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms20163877) (peroxisomes in immune response and inflammation)
right: **[Multiple sclerosis](#/diseases/brain-nerve/multiple-sclerosis-ms):** peroxisome loss in oligodendrocytes, the cells that make myelin, triggers demyelination, a hallmark of MS ([Martinović 2023](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40478-023-01595-w)).

**[Brain and nerve disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** the microglial sensitivity to peroxisomal dysfunction seen in ALD now has direct support in Alzheimer's disease: the peroxisomal beta-oxidation enzyme MFE-2 is reduced in microglia from patients and from model mice, and removing it from microglia drives inflammation and amyloid deposition ([Gao 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41162676/)). For Parkinson's disease and MS this remains a hypothesis.

parts.label: Antiviral alarm system
parts.text: An adaptor protein called MAVS, which relays signals from virus-sensing proteins, sits on both peroxisomes and mitochondria. The peroxisomal pool switches on a fast first wave of antiviral defense genes without waiting for interferon, ahead of the slower, interferon-driven response from mitochondria.
left: Whether patients with PBDs are more susceptible to viral infection has not been systematically studied; the human literature is limited to isolated case reports, and those describe bacterial or opportunistic infection. Experiments that placed MAVS only on peroxisomes showed that peroxisomal MAVS alone can launch this fast response ([Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/)).
furtherReading: [Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/) (discovery of peroxisomal MAVS signaling)
[Odendall 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24952503/) (peroxisomal MAVS drives type III interferon)
[Ferreira 2022](http://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0962892421001999) (review of how viruses exploit peroxisomes)
right: **[Viral infection:](#/diseases/infection)** peroxisomes act as an early antiviral alarm, switching on defense genes that slow infection before the full immune response arrives ([Dixit 2010](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20451243/)).

**[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** flaviviruses, HIV, SARS-CoV-2 and others shrink peroxisomes to silence this early warning system ([Zhang 2018](https://journals.asm.org/doi/10.1128/jvi.01677-17)).

label: Metabolic Signaling
summary: two PPAR-targeting drugs, elafibranor and seladelpar, received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for PBC.
description: Peroxisomes are part of a fat-sensing loop, not only a factory. A family of proteins in the cell nucleus called PPARs (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors) detect fats, including some made or processed in peroxisomes, and switch on fat-burning machinery, including peroxisomal enzymes. This loop helps decide how much fat the body burns versus stores.

parts.label: Pan-PPAR signaling
parts.text: Pan-PPAR drugs act on several PPAR family members at once. Lanifibranor has been studied in clinical trials for fatty liver disease (MASH).
left: **[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (indirect)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** several of the fats that activate PPARs are made or broken down in peroxisomes, so when peroxisomes fail, this signaling loop is disrupted as a downstream consequence rather than a primary cause. Of the seven mechanisms, this one has the weakest direct genetic link.
furtherReading: [Gonzalez 2008](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18006136/) (the "peroxisome proliferation" that gave PPARs appears to be unique to rodents)
right: **[Liver disease](#/diseases/liver):** lanifibranor has been studied in clinical trials for MASH (fatty liver disease with inflammation) and two PPAR-targeting drugs, elafibranor and seladelpar, received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis. The share of their benefit that runs through peroxisomes is not known.

parts.label: PPARα (fibrates, pemafibrate)
parts.text: PPARα is the most established drug target in this family. It switches on peroxisomal and mitochondrial fat-burning genes and is targeted clinically to lower triglycerides.
left: **[Peroxisome Biogenesis Disorders (indirect)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** as with pan-PPAR signaling, the link is downstream of failed peroxisomal fat metabolism rather than a primary cause.
furtherReading: [Gonzalez 2008](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18006136/) (review of PPARα signaling and peroxisome proliferation)
right: **[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** PPARα activation, exercise and fasting enhance peroxisomal function in fat tissue and liver, improving fat burning ([Jiang 2022](https://e-dmj.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.4093/dmj.2021.0274)).

**[Cancer](#/diseases/cancer):** AMACR and other PPAR-regulated genes link peroxisomal lipid metabolism to tumor growth; anti-cancer PPAR antagonists may expose peroxisomal vulnerabilities ([Kong 2020](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2020.00153/full)).
**Heart disease:** fibrates lower triglycerides, but pemafibrate did not reduce cardiovascular events in a large outcome trial ([Das Pradhan 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36342113/)).

parts.label: PPARγ (pioglitazone)
parts.text: PPARγ controls fat cell development and insulin sensitivity. The PPARγ agonist pioglitazone is used clinically in type 2 diabetes.
left: **[X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** leriglitazone, a brain-penetrant PPARγ agonist, has been studied in clinical trials in adults with X-ALD.
furtherReading: [Vales-Villamarin 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2021.763853/full) (PPARγ variants and drugs affect insulin sensitivity and diabetes risk)
[Steinke 2023](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/12/8/1116) (PPARγ agonists rescue cognition in Alzheimer's models)
right: **[Type 2 diabetes](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** genetic variants and drugs that activate PPARγ affect insulin sensitivity and diabetes risk ([Vales-Villamarin 2022](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2021.763853/full)).

**[Alzheimer's disease](#/diseases/brain-nerve/alzheimers-disease):** PPARγ agonists rescue cognition in animal models, but a peroxisome-driven mechanism is unproven ([Steinke 2023](https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4409/12/8/1116)).

label: Peroxisome Biogenesis & Recycling
summary: how cells build new peroxisomes, stock them with enzymes, and recycle the worn-out ones
description: Peroxisomes turn over within days, so cells constantly build new ones, stock them with enzymes, and clear out damaged ones. This mechanism is foundational: when it fails, every other peroxisomal function fails with it.

parts.label: Import (address-tag delivery)
parts.text: Every enzyme a peroxisome uses is made in the cytosol and carried in through the membrane. Each carries a short address tag (PTS1 or PTS2) that a shuttle receptor reads: PEX5 for PTS1, and PEX7 together with PEX5 for PTS2.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum disorders](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** variants in PEX1, PEX6, PEX26, PEX10 and other PEX genes disrupt this import and assembly system, so peroxisomes are not built, or are built empty, and every peroxisomal function fails together.
**[RCDP type 1](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** loss of PEX7 blocks only PTS2 cargo, which explains why plasmalogen synthesis and alpha-oxidation fail while most other functions are spared.
furtherReading: [Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/) (PH1 enzyme mistargeting)
[Waterham 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26611709/) (overview of peroxisomal disorders)
[Feng 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35768507/) (structure of the PEX2/PEX10/PEX12 channel that recycles PEX5)
[Fujiki 2020](https://doi.org/10.1242/jcs.236943) (recent insights into peroxisome biogenesis and associated diseases)
[Honsho 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-60204-8_4) (peroxisome biogenesis disorders)
right: **[Kidney disease](#/diseases/kidney):** primary hyperoxaluria type 1 can be a subtler failure of this system: in some patients a single variant changes the address tag so a working AGXT enzyme is sent to mitochondria instead of peroxisomes ([Danpure 2006](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17027096/)).

**[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** the import system declines with age, reducing import of catalase and fat-burning enzymes and triggering stress pathways ([Kim 2024](https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/3/10/pgae429/7793200)).
**[Neurodegeneration](#/diseases/brain-nerve):** PEX5 import defects compromise ROS detoxification ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Diabetes](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** functional peroxisomes are required for insulin-producing beta-cell integrity; when import fails, beta-cells die even without obvious oxidative stress ([Baboota 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30795913/)).

parts.label: Division
parts.text: Peroxisomes divide to multiply, expanding their numbers as the cell's needs change. PEX11B elongates the membrane, and fission proteins shared with mitochondria (DRP1, MFF, FIS1) pinch it in two.
left: **[PEX11B deficiency](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** a mild PBD with cataracts, hearing loss and short stature, often with normal standard blood tests ([Ebberink 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22581968/)).

**[DRP1 (DNM1L) and MFF deficiencies](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** these break both peroxisome and mitochondrial division, producing elongated organelles and severe neurological disease ([Waterham 2007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17460227/)).
furtherReading: [Schrader 2015b](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25687155/) (peroxisome division in health and disease)
right: **[Diabetic neuropathy](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** excess fat chemically modifies PEX11B, blocking peroxisome formation in Schwann cells and driving nerve damage ([Yang 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39934809/)).
**[Viral infection](#/diseases/infection):** infection reshapes peroxisome size, number and positioning over time ([Knoblach 2021](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.E21-02-0074)).
**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** peroxisome number and function rise as fat cells mature ([Park 2019](https://www.jci.org/articles/view/120606)).

parts.label: Recycling (pexophagy)
parts.text: Worn-out or excess peroxisomes are tagged with ubiquitin, engulfed by autophagy and digested so their components can be reused.
left: **[Zellweger spectrum (PEX1 variants)](#/diseases/genetic-disorders):** in cells with impaired PEX1, ubiquitin-tagged PEX5 builds up on the peroxisome and marks it for destruction, so excess pexophagy contributes to peroxisome loss; blocking pexophagy restored peroxisome function in patient cells ([Law 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28521612/)). This points to a possible therapeutic route.
furtherReading: [Zhang 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26344566/) (oxidative stress triggers pexophagy through ATM and PEX5)
[Law 2017](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28521612/) (how the peroxisomal AAA ATPase complex prevents runaway pexophagy)
[Li 2021](https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2021.814047) (the peroxisome-autophagy redox connection)
right: **[Aging](#/diseases/aging):** quality-control systems clear damaged peroxisomes, preventing them from becoming sources of oxidative damage; these pathways decline with age ([Jo 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s12276-020-00503-9)).

**[Obesity](#/diseases/obesity-diabetes):** the peroxisomal E3 ligase PEX2, which marks proteins for destruction, is stabilized by peroxisome-derived ROS in fat tissue ([Ding 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8688145/)).
